name: Perth Arena
key_features: Angular facade panels in a jigsaw pattern wrap an arena with a retractable roof.

name: Palais Garnier
key_features: A Beaux-Arts opera whose grand staircase and foyers make a promenade as theatrical as the stage.

name: United Nations Secretariat Building
by: Wallace K. Harrison with Le Corbusier and Oscar Niemeyer
key_features: Slab tower with glass curtain-wall long faces and windowless stone-clad ends beside the East River.

name: Maisons Jaoul
key_features: Two brick houses with exposed concrete beams and low Catalan vaults, some topped with grass.

name: Port House
key_features: A faceted glass extension, shaped like a ship's bow, hovers on concrete piers above an old fire station.

name: Torre de Collserola
key_features: A slim concrete shaft held upright by tensioned guy cables carries a stack of triangular decks.

name: Miho Museum
key_features: Approach through a tunnel and over a cable-stayed bridge to glass-roofed halls set into a mountain.

name: Fernsehturm Berlin
by: Hermann Henselmann, Fritz Dieter and Günter Franke
key_features: A tapering concrete shaft carries a steel-clad sphere holding a viewing deck and revolving restaurant.

name: Stadio San Nicola
key_features: Upper stands split into concrete petals with gaps between, floating over a bowl set in an earth bank.

name: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden
key_features: A hollow concrete drum raised on four piers rings a fountain court beside a sunken sculpture garden.

name: NEMO Science Museum
key_features: A copper-green hull rises from the harbour over a road tunnel, its sloping roof a public stepped square.

name: Museum für Moderne Kunst
key_features: A wedge-shaped 'piece of cake' plan fills a triangular site, with galleries around a toplit hall.

name: Oscar Niemeyer Museum
key_features: A raised eye-shaped gallery on a single yellow pier above a pool, beside an earlier long concrete block.

name: Immeuble Clarté
key_features: Dry-assembled steel-framed flats with full-height glazing, duplexes and glass-block stair landings.

name: Pinakothek der Moderne
key_features: A central rotunda under a glazed dome links four museums along top-lit gallery axes.

name: Fountain Place
by: Henry N. Cobb (Pei Cobb Freed & Partners)
key_features: Faceted green-glass prism tower over a Dan Kiley water garden of cypress trees and fountains.

name: Weisman Art Museum
key_features: Plain brick box to the campus, a cascade of folded stainless steel forms facing the river.

name: Soreq Nuclear Research Center
key_features: Battered concrete reactor block fronting a colonnaded courtyard with a long reflecting pool.

name: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
by: Alvar and Elissa Aalto with Jean-Jacques Baruël
key_features: Roof monitors bounce daylight off curved reflectors into white galleries set in a wooded hollow.

name: Knights of Columbus Building
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: Four round brick-clad corner towers carry exposed steel spandrel beams spanning between them.

name: Natural History Museum
key_features: Romanesque front of terracotta moulded with plants and animals; iron-and-glass roof over the main hall.

name: One Chase Manhattan Plaza (28 Liberty Street)
key_features: Steel-and-aluminium slab with columns outside the skin, on a plaza with a sunken Noguchi garden.

name: Kitakyushu Central Library
key_features: Two long copper-clad concrete barrel vaults bend across the site, bringing daylight into the reading rooms.

name: Mole Antonelliana
key_features: A steep square masonry dome rises from a temple-like base into a slender spire.

name: National Museum of the American Indian
key_features: Curving tiers of rough limestone evoke wind-carved rock around a domed central gathering space.

name: Pinacoteca Giovanni e Marella Agnelli
key_features: A steel 'treasure chest' gallery perched on the rooftop test track of the Lingotto car factory.

name: Nordic House
key_features: Low white building under a blue-glazed tiled roof whose folded profile echoes the mountains.

name: Shizuoka Press and Broadcasting Center
key_features: Office boxes cantilever from a single cylindrical concrete core, leaving gaps for future growth.

name: Salerno Maritime Terminal
key_features: A flowing concrete shell like an oyster, its ramps leading passengers from ticket hall to quay.

name: McLaren Technology Centre
key_features: A semicircular glass building wrapped around a formal lake, with a long internal boulevard along its curve.

name: Yamanashi Press and Broadcasting Centre
key_features: Concrete cylinder towers carry floors bridged between them, with gaps left for future growth.

name: Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower
key_features: An elliptical tower of schools wrapped in a white web of curving diagonal bands, like a cocoon.

name: Palazzo Lombardia
key_features: Sinuous office ribbons wrap a central tower and enclose a covered public piazza.

name: Tokyo Tower
key_features: A steel lattice tower painted in international orange and white, modelled on the Eiffel Tower.

name: Torre Emperador Castellana (Torre Espacio)
key_features: A square plan at the base morphs into two curved faces as the glass tower rises.

name: Solow Building
key_features: Travertine-edged glass curtain walls sweep down in concave curves to the street on two faces.

name: Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre
key_features: A white dome, a curved auditorium and a slim tower stand on an open riverside plaza.

name: Kunsthalle Bielefeld
key_features: A compact cubic block clad in red sandstone, set beside a sculpture garden.

name: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center
by: I. M. Pei & Partners (James Ingo Freed)
key_features: A dark glass skin on a vast steel space frame encloses the halls and a crystal-palace-like lobby.

name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
key_features: Venetian-style palazzo of galleries wrapped around a glass-roofed garden courtyard.

name: Kyoto National Museum
key_features: Brick Meiji-era hall in French baroque style, an early Western-style museum in Japan.

name: Kobe Port Tower
key_features: Red steel-pipe lattice tower in a hyperboloid hourglass form standing on the harbour.

name: Kingdom Centre
key_features: Tapering tower crowned by an open parabolic arch with a skybridge spanning its top.

name: Tour Duo
key_features: Two leaning glass towers of different heights share a base beside the railway tracks.

name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
key_features: Massive stepped stone monument over a pool, with a crypt of giant guardians and a domed hall.

name: National Museum of Finland
key_features: Church-like asymmetric massing and a tall tower blend Finnish medieval and national romantic motifs.

name: National Museum of Ethnology
key_features: Clustered gallery blocks around a central courtyard, planned to grow in modular units.

name: Wangjing SOHO
key_features: Three mountain-like towers wrapped in continuous flowing bands of white aluminium and glass.

name: Philadelphia City Hall
key_features: Load-bearing masonry block around a central court, its tower crowned by a statue of William Penn.

name: Lipstick Building
key_features: Oval tower of red granite and steel bands that steps back twice like an extending lipstick.

name: Humboldt Forum
key_features: Rebuilt baroque palace fronts on three sides, with a plain stone grid facing the river.

name: Makuhari Messe
key_features: Long wave-shaped metal roof spans column-free exhibition halls beside a separate event hall.

name: Spittelau Viaducts Housing
key_features: Angled housing blocks stride over and between Otto Wagner's railway viaduct arches by the canal.

name: Teatre Nacional de Catalunya
key_features: A glass-walled classical temple of concrete columns and pediment fronts the theatre halls.

name: House with Chimaeras
key_features: Art Nouveau house on a steep slope, its facades crowded with cast-concrete animals and sea creatures.

name: Red City Hall (Rotes Rathaus)
key_features: Red brick town hall in Italian Renaissance style, with a tall central clock tower and a terracotta frieze.

name: Lille Cathedral
by: Charles Leroy; west front by Pierre-Louis Carlier
key_features: Neo-Gothic cathedral finished with a modern west front of thin translucent marble hung on a steel frame.

name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
key_features: Neo-Baroque bath palace wrapped around large open-air pools fed by thermal springs.

name: Museum of Jewish Heritage
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: A hexagonal granite building with a stepped pyramidal roof on the harbour edge of Battery Park City.

name: Pierre Lassonde Pavilion
key_features: Stacked glass gallery boxes shrink and cantilever as they rise, stepping out over a street and park.

name: Museum Folkwang
key_features: Pavilions and courtyards linked by glazed walkways, clad in translucent panels of recycled glass.

name: High Museum of Art
key_features: White enamel-panelled galleries wrap a quarter-circle atrium lit from above and climbed by ramps.

name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
key_features: A glass tent-like atrium leans on a white tower with cantilevered drum and box volumes over the lake.

name: Museum of Modern Art
key_features: Galleries layered around a tall atrium look onto the sculpture garden through refined glass and stone.

name: Pergamon Museum
key_features: A three-winged neoclassical block built around reconstructed ancient monuments like the Pergamon Altar.

name: Museum of Pop Culture
key_features: Colourful blobs of painted aluminium and stainless steel shingles flow around the passing monorail.

name: Saint Louis Art Museum, East Building
key_features: Low pavilion of dark polished concrete with a deep coffered ceiling that admits daylight.

name: Kurashiki City Art Museum (former City Hall)
key_features: Heavy concrete beams stacked like a log storehouse; Tange's former city hall now holds galleries.

name: Hearst Castle
key_features: Spanish Revival main house with twin bell towers above terraces, pools and guest cottages.

name: Mikhailovsky Palace (Russian Museum)
key_features: Neoclassical palace with a Corinthian portico behind a forecourt, set on the square Rossi planned with it.

name: State Historical Museum
key_features: Red brick Russian Revival museum with tent-roofed towers closing the north end of Red Square.

name: Vienna City Hall
key_features: Neo-Gothic town hall with a tall central tower over arcaded courtyards, facing a park on the Ringstrasse.

name: Marin County Civic Center
key_features: Long arcaded wings under a blue roof bridge between hills, meeting at a dome beside a gold spire.

name: St Peter's Church, Klippan
key_features: Dark brick, never cut, forms floor, walls and vaults; a split steel column holds the roof in the dim nave.

name: National Gallery of Art, East Building
key_features: A trapezoid site split into two triangles, with knife-edge marble corners and a skylit triangular atrium.

name: Kresge Auditorium
key_features: One-eighth of a sphere: a thin concrete shell resting on three points, with glass walls between.

name: Sanatorium Purkersdorf
key_features: Flat-roofed white cube on a concrete frame, with flush windows edged in blue-and-white chequer tiles.

name: MIT Chapel
key_features: Brick cylinder in a moat: water light glints through low arches, a skylight falls on Bertoia's metal screen.

name: Galeries Lafayette Berlin
key_features: Glass department store cored by two glass cones that reflect daylight down through every floor.

name: Geisel Library
key_features: Reading floors stack out like an inverted stepped pyramid on splayed concrete piers above a glazed base.

name: Maison du Peuple, Clichy
key_features: Prefabricated light steel panels, a sliding roof and a movable floor let a market turn into a hall.

name: Netherlands Pavilion, Expo 2000
key_features: Stacked Dutch landscapes, from dunes and flowers to a forest floor, pile up into a vertical park.

name: Kagawa Prefectural Government Office
key_features: Concrete balcony beam-ends echo timber joinery on every floor of the tower above an open pilotis lobby.

name: Marugame Genichiro-Inokuma Museum of Contemporary Art (MIMOCA)
key_features: A deep canopied forecourt facing the station is backed by a vast facade wall carrying Inokuma's mural.

name: Keeling House
key_features: Four maisonette towers fan out like butterfly wings from a central service core linked by bridges.

name: Immeuble Molitor
key_features: A glass and glass-block facade on a party-wall flat block, topped by Le Corbusier's vaulted studio home.

name: Villa Schwob (Villa Turque)
key_features: Concrete frame clad in brick, with apsidal side bays and a famous blank panel on the street front.

name: French Communist Party Headquarters
key_features: A curving glass office wall rises behind a white dome capping an underground assembly hall.

name: IKMZ Library, BTU Cottbus
key_features: An amoeba-plan tower wrapped in glass printed with overlapping letters, with a brightly coloured spiral stair.

name: Kentuck Knob
key_features: A hexagon-module Usonian house of local sandstone and cypress under an overhanging copper roof.

name: Humana Building
key_features: A layered granite tower with a colonnaded loggia at its base and a cantilevered terrace high up.

name: Maison Hermès
key_features: A skin of custom glass blocks glows like a lantern, its frame designed to flex in earthquakes.

name: Haus des Rundfunks
key_features: A long dark clinker-brick front wraps a triangular plan, with the sound studios shielded inside it.

name: Mäusebunker
key_features: A battleship-like concrete wedge of sloped walls bristling with blue ventilation pipes and angled windows.

name: Maria Regina Martyrum
key_features: A high grey wall encloses a memorial forecourt; the church sits as a raised box above a lower crypt.

name: Muuratsalo Experimental House
key_features: Courtyard walls patched with dozens of brick and tile test panels around a central fire pit.

name: Rødovre Town Hall
key_features: A precise curtain-wall slab with dark end walls; inside, a stair hangs from thin steel rods.

name: Villa Göth
key_features: Bare brick walls and exposed concrete beams left raw inside: the house that prompted the word brutalism.

name: Monte Amiata Housing (Gallaratese)
key_features: Red blocks gather around open-air theatres, beside Rossi's long white gallery block on blade walls.

name: Torre de la Creu
key_features: Interlocking cylinders capped by trencadís-tiled domes, one rising as a tower crowned by a cross.
